answer: Practically, the chain should mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because saffron only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, pigment is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any relic approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
